MARKE.|97}}</noinclude>vvere other boates vvith him. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=37}}† And there arose a great storme of vvinde, and the vvaues bette into the boate, so that the boate vvas filled. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=38}}† And he vvas in the hinder part of the boate sleeping vpon a pillovv: and they raise him, and say to him, Maister, doth it not pertaine to thee that vve perish? {{verse|chapter=4|verse=39}}† And rising vp he threatened the vvinde, and said to the sea, Peace, be stil. And the vvinde ceased: and there vvas made a great calme. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=40}}† And he said to them, Why are you feareful? neither yet haue you faith? And they feared vvith great feare: and they said one to an other, Who is this (thinkest thou) that both vvinde and sea obey him?

{{c|{{larger|A N N O T A T I O N S}}}}
{{c|{{sc|Chap. IIII.}}}}

''12. Lest they should be conuerted.''] {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=God is not author of sinne, but mans owne will.}}These speaches here and els where, we must not so vnderstand as though he spake in parables of purpose and to this end, that the hearers might not vnderstand, lest they should be conuerted: which were as much to say as that he would not haue them vnderstand, nor be conuerted: but we must learne the true sense of this very place in S. Matthew {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 13.''}}and in the Actes, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Act. 28.''}}where our Sauiour and S. Paul speake thus, ''They haue heard heauily, and haue shut their eies, lest perhaps they may see, and vnderstand, and be conuerted, and I heale them''. Whereby it is euident, that the speaking in parables was not the cause (for many beside the Apostles heard and vnderstood) but them selues would not heare, and vnderstand, and be conuerted: and so were the cause of their owne wilful and obstinate infidelity. And therfore also he spake in parables, because they were not worthy to vnderstand, as the other to whom he expounded them.

''27. And sleepe.''] The Church, and Christs doctrine, (sleepe we, wake we) increaseth by the great prouidence of God. only the preachers must sow, and plant, and water, and {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''1. Cor. 3''.}}* God wil giue the increase, nourishing the seede in mens harts. And therfore we may not giue ouer, or be impatient and solicitous, if we haue not alwaies good successe: but doing our duty, commit the rest to God.

''31. Mustard seed.''] {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Church visibly increasing.}}If the Church and Truth had more and more decaied and been obscured after the Apostles time vnto ours, as the Heretikes hold: then had it been great in the beginning, and smal afterward: where this Parable saith contrary, that it was a mustard seed first, and afterward a great tree. ''vide Chrys. to. 5 contra Gentiles in vita S. Babylæ Mart''.

''32. The birdes.''] {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Christian religion wonderfully spreading.}}Of al sectes or doctrine, Christs religion at the beginning was the smallest, and most contemptible: but the successe thereof farre passed al mans doctrine: in so much that afterward al the wisest and greatest of the world made their residence and rest therein.

{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. V.}}}}}}

{{c|''To the Gerasens (and in them to al men) Christ manifesteth how the Diuel of his malice would vse them, if he would permitte: 17 and yet they like not their Sauiours presence. 21 A Woman Gentil, that began her sicknesse when the Iewes daughter began her life (signifying Abrahams time) he cureth by the way as he was comming to heale the Iewes: And euen then the Iewes do die, but yet them also he wil reuiue, as here the Iewes daughter.''}}<noinclude>{{rh||N|AND}}</noinclude>
